encounters.cc: Acutely worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea

lines: Acutely worsening shortness of breath and orthopnea

The patient is a 69-year-old male with known ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction, coronary artery disease status post myocardial infarction, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma, history of urothelial carcinoma of the bladder, small cell lung cancer of the right upper lobe, and Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome who presents with acutely worsening respiratory symptoms.
He was previously evaluated for bladder cancer in January 2020, diagnosed with lung cancer in September 2020, and developed Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome by March 2021.
He states that symptoms initially began months ago with mild breathlessness during exercise, such as walking up a hill or carrying groceries.
Over time, he began to feel short of breath performing basic tasks like showering or dressing, and now he becomes winded simply moving from one room to another in his home.
He reports that he currently sleeps with three pillows under his head and often wakes up gasping for air in the middle of the night.
Over the past three days, his legs have become increasingly swollen, and he has noticed tightness in his shoes by the afternoon.
He denies chest pain, fever, or cough.
He has also felt more fatigued, occasionally dizzy when standing, and finds it difficult to eat full meals due to early satiety and bloating.
He notes that for the past two days, he has felt as though his breathing becomes worse when lying flat, forcing him to sleep upright in a recliner.
He denies hemoptysis, wheezing, or known lung disease.
- Non-small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction
- Coronary artery disease status post myocardial infarction
- History of pulmonary tuberculosis (treated, inactive cavitary lesions)
- Small cell lung cancer, right upper lobe
He mentions that he had a heart attack "several years ago" but doesn’t recall what treatment was done.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (date and details unknown)
He has not taken his medications regularly due to cost and admits to not refilling his prescriptions in over a month.
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours PRN
- Oxycodone 5 mg oral every 6 hours PRN pain
He has smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years and drinks alcohol occasionally.
On arrival, he appears mildly distressed and is breathing rapidly.
He has a mildly elevated jugular venous pressure and bilateral pitting edema of the lower extremities to the mid-shin.
Lung auscultation reveals bilateral basilar crackles without wheezing.
His breathing worsens when lying flat for the exam.
There are no signs of infection, and cardiac auscultation reveals a displaced point of maximal impulse.
Chest x-ray demonstrates bilateral vascular congestion and small pleural effusions.
ECG shows sinus tachycardia with Q waves in the inferior leads.

encounters.cc: Acute worsening lower back pain, leg weakness, and urinary retention

lines: Acute worsening lower back pain, leg weakness, and urinary retention

The patient is a 69-year-old male with a history of metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma, small cell lung cancer, and Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome who presents to the Emergency Department with acute worsening lower back pain.
He reports that the pain began as a dull ache in the lumbar region, but has progressively increased in intensity and is now associated with shooting pains down both legs.
He also notes recent difficulty initiating urination and a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying.
Over the past two days, he has developed numbness in the inner thighs and buttocks.
